job: JOB 40: weathering and variation on the deepslate wall field

job: JOB 3: timber piers - weathered grain and a capital course

job: JOB 6: lanterns hung in the shaft and behind the window glazing
why: Small lanterns now hang inside the window heads and along the glass shaft, echoing the concept's warm interior lights, and they are tiny and well placed without cluttering the facade or breaking the silhouette, though the effect is subtle.

The change adds thin dark-grey slab lintels under the upper window sills that are barely visible and lack any hood profile or depth, so it neither clutters nor noticeably brings the build closer to the concept.

The flat plank slabs under the upper windows become stepped, bracketed sills with visible depth and shadow, matching the projecting timber sills in the concept, and they stay in the same timber tone without breaking the silhouette.

Small lanterns now hang on brackets beside the entrance columns and sit as warm accents above the first-floor windows, matching the concept's wall lanterns, and they are subtle enough not to clutter the silhouette.

job: JOB 12: heavy cornice with dentils and string course
why: The cornice job adds only a faint darker band and a few projecting blocks along the roofline, which is barely visible at this scale and doesn't produce the heavy dentilled cornice and string course seen in the concept, though it causes no harm to the silhouette or colours.

job: JOB 25: potted trees inside porch bays
why: The change adds two thin, flat green strips inside the side porch bays; they echo the concept's planters in spirit but read as small, ambiguous slivers rather than potted trees, so there's little real gain in crafting or fidelity, and nothing is harmed.

The wooden corbel brackets under each balcony slab add depth and structural logic to the flat side wall, echoing the concept's balconies, without breaking the silhouette or clashing in colour.

job: JOB 31: timber colonnettes under the balconies
why: Thin timber colonnettes now run under each balcony slab, which adds believable structural support and vertical rhythm in a matching wood tone. They are slight and slightly sparse, but they cause no silhouette damage or colour clash.

Small warm lantern pairs now sit beside the side-wall windows and near the lower stair, adding concept-matching lit accents with a bit of depth, though they are tiny and subtle and don't disturb the silhouette.

The stark black full-height void strip is replaced by a subtle dark downpipe that blends into the deepslate wall, removing a jarring slot and matching the concept's quiet vertical drainpipe beside the glass shaft.

job: JOB 35: quartz cap and string courses on the shaft
why: The pale quartz cap and string course read as a clean stone band across the shaft window head, adding the horizontal profile the concept's trim has, with no clutter or colour clash against the dark deepslate and glass.
